title: Patient Financial Assistance Program: Job-Loss and Benefit Disregards From Annual Household Income
content:
**Rule.** For a case under the Patient Financial Assistance Program, a benefit disregard is taken off the annual household income together with the laboratory-payments deduction, by the benefit documents received for the case: a case whose most recently received unemployment benefit statement is dated no more than 60 days before the application date takes off the job-loss disregard of $1000.00; a case without such a recent statement but with a Social Security benefit letter received takes off the benefit disregard of $500.00; any other case takes off no disregard. The countable income that results is never below zero.

## Points of judgement

1. **Which statement is read.** The unemployment benefit statement most recently received for the case, and the date printed on it, counted in calendar days to the application date.
2. **Recency boundary.** A statement dated 60 calendar days before the application date qualifies; one dated 61 days before does not.
3. **An older unemployment statement and a Social Security benefit letter.** The statement is not recent, so the letter governs: $500.00.
4. **A recent unemployment statement and a Social Security benefit letter.** The recent statement governs: $1000.00. The two disregards are not both taken.
5. **Neither document received.** No disregard.

## Dated cases (hypothetical; application date 1 June 2026)

| Documents received for the case | Disregard |
|---|---|
| Unemployment benefit statement dated 2 April 2026 (60 days before) | $1000.00 |
| Unemployment benefit statement dated 1 April 2026 (61 days before), no Social Security letter | None |
| Unemployment benefit statement dated 1 April 2026 and a Social Security benefit letter | $500.00 |
| Social Security benefit letter only | $500.00 |
